title: Cap. VIII Arg. 4: will to show wrath (Rom. 9:22) said to presuppose sins as cause of reprobation
latin: Apostolus dicit Deum, cum reprobat, velle ostendere iram et vindictam, etc. Rom. ix. 22. At voluntas inferendi vindictam praesupponit hominem considerari a Deo ut peccatis obstrictum: Ergo peccata reproborum, quibus obstricti moriuntur, sunt causa reprobationis.
pass_a: The Apostle says that God, when he reprobates, wills to show wrath and vengeance, etc. Rom. 9:22. But the will of inflicting vengeance presupposes that a man be considered by God as bound by sins: Therefore the sins of the reprobate, by which they die bound, are the cause of reprobation.
pass_b: Fourth: the Apostle says that when God reprobates he wills to show wrath and vengeance (Rom. 9:22). But the will to inflict vengeance presupposes that God regards a man as bound by sins. Therefore the sins by which the reprobate die bound are the cause of reprobation.

lemmas.gloss: vengeance presupposes man bound by sins

title: Cap. VIII Arg. 4 Resp.: negative reprobation not for damning; Cajetan; riches of mercy (Rom. 9:23)
latin: Si de negativa illa reprobatione sermo habeatur qua Deus firmiter decrevit singularis alicujus personae, puta Caini aut Judae, non eatenus misereri, ut velit illum efficaciter e statu peccati et miseriae eruere, ac simul decrevit permittere ejusdem in peccatis suis finalem indurationem; nego hoc fieri a Deo ob eum finem ut vindicandi sive damnandi propositum expleat. Non male hac de re philosophatur Cajetanus in Commentariis suis ad 1am Aquinatis, qu. 23. art. 5, ubi dicit, Deum non permittere peccata ut puniat, sed permittere et punire propter relucentiam justitiae suae. Quinetiam ipse Apostolus loco citato indicavit nobis, Deum specialem hanc misericordiam aliquibus negare, atque inde permittere ut indurentur (qua in re consistit negativa reprobatio) non intentione primaria damnandi hosce sic praeteritos, sed Manifestandi divitias misericordiae suae erga ipsos electos, Rom. ix. 23. Nam tum demum intelligunt electi se fuisse pura et mera Dei misericordia salvatos, cum constet denegatam fuisse aliis illam vocationem secundum propositum quae ipsis ex gratuito Dei beneplacito fuit concessa; cum constet illos nihilo fuisse meliores hisce praeteritis quoad conditionem naturae corruptae, in qua specialis misericordia eos deprehendit; denique cum constet eos futuros fuisse non minus induratos ipsis reprobis, nisi ex mero Dei favore hac speciali gratia fuissent emolliti.
pass_a: If speech be had concerning that negative reprobation by which God firmly decreed of some singular person, for example of Cain or Judas, not so far to have mercy as to will efficaciously to draw him out of the state of sin and misery, and at the same time decreed to permit the final hardening of the same in his sins: I deny that this is done by God for that end, that he may fulfill a purpose of avenging or of damning. Not badly does Cajetan philosophize on this matter in his Commentaries on the First of Aquinas, question 23, article 5, where he says that God does not permit sins that he may punish, but permits and punishes on account of the shining forth of his justice. Moreover the Apostle himself in the place cited has indicated to us that God denies this special mercy to some, and thence permits that they be hardened (in which matter negative reprobation consists) not with primary intention of damning these thus passed by, but of Manifesting the riches of his mercy toward the elect themselves, Rom. 9:23. For then at last the elect understand that they were saved by the pure and mere mercy of God, when it is established that that calling according to purpose which was granted them from the gratuitous good pleasure of God was denied to others; when it is established that they were in no way better than these passed by as to the condition of corrupted nature, in which special mercy seized them; finally when it is established that they would have been no less hardened than the reprobate themselves, unless from the mere favor of God they had been softened by this special grace.
pass_b: If we speak of that negative reprobation by which God firmly decreed of some particular person — say Cain or Judas — not so far to have mercy as to will to draw him efficaciously out of sin and misery, and at the same time decreed to permit his final hardening in sin: I deny God does this to fulfill a purpose of vengeance or damnation. Cajetan puts it well on Aquinas I, q. 23 a. 5: God does not permit sins in order to punish, but permits and punishes for the shining forth of his justice. Paul himself in the cited place shows that God denies this special mercy to some and so permits them to be hardened — wherein negative reprobation consists — not with primary intent to damn those thus passed by, but to manifest the riches of his mercy toward the elect (Rom. 9:23). Only then do the elect see they were saved by pure mere mercy: when it is plain that the calling according to purpose granted them by gratuitous good pleasure was denied to others; that they were no better than those passed by as to corrupt nature, in which special mercy found them; and that they would have been no less hardened than the reprobate unless mere divine favor had softened them by that special grace.

lemmas.gloss: permit and punish for justice's shining

title: Cap. VIII Arg. 4 Resp.: will to punish follows foresight final perseverance — not cause of negative reprobation
latin: Est igitur verum, Deum velle ostendere iram et vindictam in omnes reprobatos: sed haec voluntas vindictae inferendae cum reprobatione illa negativa sive non-electione, de qua disputamus, non est immediate conjuncta, sed exoritur ex praeviso interventu finalis perseverantiae in peccato: qui status omnium reproborum infallibiliter futurus praevidetur a Deo ut eventus consequens negativam reprobationem, non ut causa antecedens. Est igitur parum firma argumentatio, Deus reprobans homines, vult eosdem etiam punire, Ergo reprobationis negativae causa est peccatum praevisum.
pass_a: It is therefore true that God wills to show wrath and vengeance upon all the reprobated: but this will of inflicting vengeance is not immediately joined with that negative reprobation or non-election about which we dispute, but arises from the foresighted intervention of final perseverance in sin: which state of all the reprobate as infallibly future is foresighted by God as an event consequent upon negative reprobation, not as an antecedent cause. The argumentation is therefore little firm: God reprobating men wills also to punish the same, Therefore the cause of negative reprobation is foresighted sin.
pass_b: True: God wills to show wrath and vengeance on all the reprobate. But that will to inflict vengeance is not immediately joined to the negative reprobation or non-election we are disputing. It arises from foresighted intervention of final perseverance in sin — a state of all the reprobate foresighted by God as infallibly future as an event consequent on negative reprobation, not as an antecedent cause. So the argument is weak: God in reprobating also wills to punish them; therefore foresighted sin is the cause of negative reprobation.

lemmas.gloss: will-to-punish does not prove foresight cause

title: Cap. VIII Arg. 5: Jewish unbelief (Rom. 9:32; 11:19-20) said to be cause of reprobation
latin: Ex eodem Apostolo conantur demonstrare, permansionem in infidelitate esse reprobationis causam; quoniam reprobationem Judaeorum rejicit in infidelitatem eorundem tanquam causam: Rom. ix. 31, 32. Israel, inquit, sectando legem justitiae, in legem justitiae non pervenit. Quare? Quia non ex fide. Ubi indicatur solutio quaestionis de causa reprobationis Judaeorum. Quod ipsum confirmatur ex illis verbis, Rom. xi. 19, 20. Dices, Fracti sunt rami, ut ego inserar. Bene: propter incredulitatem fracti sunt: Tu autem fide stas, etc. Summa argumenti haec est: Judaei reprobati fuerunt propter perseverantiam finalem in infidelitate sua: Ergo perseverantia haec in infidelitate est causa reprobationis Divinae.
pass_a: From the same Apostle they try to demonstrate that remaining in unbelief is the cause of reprobation; since he casts back the reprobation of the Jews upon the unbelief of the same as cause: Rom. 9:31, 32. Israel, he says, pursuing the law of righteousness, did not arrive at the law of righteousness. Why? Because not of faith. Where the solution of the question concerning the cause of the reprobation of the Jews is indicated. Which itself is confirmed from those words, Rom. 11:19, 20. You will say, The branches were broken off, that I might be grafted in. Well: because of unbelief they were broken off: But you stand by faith, etc. The sum of the argument is this: The Jews were reprobated on account of final perseverance in their unbelief: Therefore this perseverance in unbelief is the cause of Divine reprobation.
pass_b: Fifth: from the same Apostle they try to prove remaining in unbelief is the cause of reprobation, since he casts the Jews' reprobation back on their unbelief as cause (Rom. 9:31-32): Israel, pursuing the law of righteousness, did not arrive at it — Why? Because not of faith. Confirmed by Rom. 11:19-20: The branches were broken off that I might be grafted in — Well: because of unbelief they were broken off; but you stand by faith. Sum: the Jews were reprobated for final perseverance in unbelief; therefore that perseverance is the cause of divine reprobation.

title: Cap. VIII Arg. 5 Resp.: Rom. 9 explains failure to attain justice, not eternal reprobation; Estius
latin: Ad primum testimonium ex nono ad Romanos petitum respondeo, Non reddi rationem cur reprobati fuerint Judaei, sed cur justitiam veram coram Deo minime sunt assecuti, utcunque videantur fuisse justitiae acerrimi sectatores. Id autem inde evenisse dicit Apostolus, quod justitiam quaerebant in operibus suis, et exacta legis observatione, spreta justificatione per fidem; cum ex operibus legis justificari sit homini per peccatum infirmato et corrupto plane impossibile, et necesse sit omni peccatori ad fidem confugere, ut coram Deo justificetur. Hanc interpretationem non modo Theologi nostri, sed etiam ex Pontificiis Gulielmus Estius Professor Duacenus expresse sequitur in Commentariis suis ad hunc ipsum locum, ubi inter alia et haec verba posuit, Scito non hic reddi rationem cur reprobati fuerint Judaei, sed cur non justitiam assecuti. Prius igitur hoc testimonium a proposito plane alienum.
pass_a: To the first testimony sought from the ninth to the Romans I answer, That a reason is not rendered why the Jews were reprobated, but why they least attained true righteousness before God, howsoever they may seem to have been most keen followers of righteousness. But the Apostle says that this happened thence, that they sought righteousness in their works, and in exact observation of the law, justification through faith having been despised; since to be justified from the works of the law is plainly impossible for a man weakened and corrupted by sin, and it is necessary that every sinner flee unto faith, that he may be justified before God. This interpretation not only our Theologians, but also among the Papists William Estius, Professor of Douai, expressly follows in his Commentaries on this very place, where among other things he also put these words, Know that here a reason is not rendered why the Jews were reprobated, but why they did not attain righteousness. This first testimony therefore is plainly alien from the purpose.
pass_b: To the first witness from Romans 9: Paul is not giving the reason why the Jews were reprobated, but why they failed to attain true righteousness before God — however keen they seemed as pursuers of righteousness. That happened, he says, because they sought righteousness in their works and exact law-keeping, despising justification by faith; justification from works of the law is plainly impossible for a man weakened and corrupted by sin, and every sinner must flee to faith to be justified before God. Not only our theologians follow this reading, but among the Romanists William Estius of Douai expressly does so on this very place: Know that here no reason is given why the Jews were reprobated, but why they did not attain righteousness. So this first testimony is plainly off the point.

lemmas.gloss: Estius: why justice missed, not why reprobated

title: Cap. VIII Arg. 5 Resp.: Rom. 11 concerns visible grafting of peoples, not eternal election of persons
latin: Neque posterius, quod in confirmationem argumenti adducitur, quicquam facit ad rem. Apostolus enim non de singularibus personis electis sed de toto corpore Judaeorum et Gentium indefinite et indiscriminatim considerato loquitur. Neque de electione et reprobatione aeterna affirmat, aliquem singularem hominem propter incredulitatem exscindi et quasi expungi e numero electorum, et denuo fide recuperata quasi postliminio inseri: sed modo Judaeos in genere sua infidelitate desiisse esse populum Dei foederatum, et Gentes amplexando fidem evangelicam in illorum locum successisse. Atque ut Gentibus adimat omnem superbiendi occasionem, ait Judaeos, si in Christum credant et in sua infidelitate persistere desinant, inserendos, hoc est, in foederatum Dei populum admittendos; Gentes autem, quae nunc gaudent nomine Ecclesiae et populi Dei, si resiliant a fide Christi, fore etiam defringendas, et a corpore Ecclesiae exscindendas. Haec interminatio in multis Gentibus effectum sortita est, quae a fide Christi ad superstitionem Mahumeticam desciscentes, a corpore Ecclesiae, hoc est, foederati Dei populi, revulsae conspiciuntur. Sed quid interim haec omnia conducunt ad probandam singularium personarum reprobationem aeternam, ex consideratione futurae illorum incredulitatis, tanquam causae motivae, profluxisse? Profecto nihil: Quia non de singularium personarum aeterna electione et reprobatione, sed de visibili Gentium insitione et defractione disserit Apostolus: quia haec insitio et defractio, cujus mentionem facit, non denotat aeternam electionem aut reprobationem singularium personarum, sed temporalem admissionem aut rejectionem alicujus gentis a statu populi foederati, quorum alterum fit mediante fide, alterum mediante infidelitate: quia ab omni sana Theologia abhorret, statuere, aliquos reprobatos fieri posse electos, aut aliquos electos reprobatos; et tamen Apostolus expresse docet hosce insitos, de quibus loquitur, posse fieri defractos, et hosce defractos posse rursus fieri insitos.
pass_a: Nor does the latter, which is brought forward in confirmation of the argument, do anything to the matter. For the Apostle speaks not of singular elect persons but of the whole body of Jews and Gentiles considered indefinitely and without discrimination. Nor does he affirm concerning eternal election and reprobation that some singular man is cut off on account of unbelief and as it were expunged from the number of the elect, and again, faith recovered, as it were by postliminium grafted in: but only that the Jews in general by their unbelief ceased to be the confederate people of God, and that the Gentiles by embracing the evangelical faith succeeded into their place. And that he may take away from the Gentiles every occasion of pride, he says that the Jews, if they believe in Christ and cease to persist in their unbelief, are to be grafted in, that is, admitted into the confederate people of God; but that the Gentiles, who now rejoice in the name of the Church and people of God, if they spring back from the faith of Christ, will also be broken off, and cut out from the body of the Church. This threat has taken effect in many Gentiles, who, defecting from the faith of Christ unto Mahometan superstition, are seen torn away from the body of the Church, that is, of the confederate people of God. But what meantime do all these things conduce to proving that the eternal reprobation of singular persons flowed from consideration of their future unbelief as moving cause? Truly nothing: Because the Apostle discourses not of the eternal election and reprobation of singular persons, but of the visible grafting and breaking off of the Gentiles: because this grafting and breaking off, of which he makes mention, does not denote the eternal election or reprobation of singular persons, but the temporal admission or rejection of some nation from the state of the confederate people, of which the one is made by means of faith, the other by means of unbelief: because it abhors from all sound Theology to establish that some reprobated can become elect, or some elect reprobated; and yet the Apostle expressly teaches that these grafted ones of whom he speaks can become broken off, and these broken off can again become grafted.
pass_b: Nor does the confirming text from Romans 11 help. Paul is not speaking of particular elect persons but of the whole body of Jews and Gentiles taken indefinitely. He is not teaching that some singular man is cut off for unbelief and struck from the number of the elect, then grafted back by recovered faith as by postliminium. He says only that the Jews in general, by unbelief, ceased to be God's covenant people, and that the Gentiles, embracing the gospel faith, succeeded into their place. To strip the Gentiles of every occasion for pride, he adds: if the Jews believe in Christ and stop persisting in unbelief, they are to be grafted in — admitted to the covenant people; and if the Gentiles who now rejoice as Church and people of God spring back from Christ's faith, they too will be broken off and cut from the Church's body. That threat has taken effect in many Gentiles who defected from Christ's faith to Mahometan superstition and stand torn from the covenant body. How does any of this prove that eternal reprobation of particular persons flowed from regard to their future unbelief as moving cause? It proves nothing. Paul discusses visible grafting and breaking of peoples, not eternal election and reprobation of individuals. That grafting and breaking denotes temporal admission or rejection of a nation from covenant status — one by faith, the other by unbelief. Sound theology abhors making reprobates into elect or elect into reprobates; yet Paul expressly teaches that those grafted of whom he speaks can be broken off, and those broken off grafted again.

lemmas.gloss: not eternal election of singular persons

title: Cap. VIII Arg. 5 Resp.: remnant according to election (Rom. 11:5, 7); reprobates left to their hardness
latin: Hisce omnibus accedat, quod cum gens aliqua, puta Judaeorum, ob infidelitatem defracta sit a corpore Ecclesiae, nemo tamen ex electis defringatur: nam, eodem Apostolo autore, reliquiae secundum electionem gratiae salvae factae sunt, Rom. xi. 5, 7. Denique, quod quidam non defringantur, aliis ex eadem gente resilientibus et pereuntibus, id evenit non quia hi electi fuerunt ex praevisa fide sua, sed quia fides data fuit hisce electis ex aeterno Dei beneplacito, et reservatio secundum electionem facta est, Rom. xi. 5. Sic etiam quod quidam defringantur, mediante sua infidelitate, et pereant, id non arguit Deum eos ab aeterno reprobasse propter praevisam infidelitatem; sed quod hi reprobati duritiae suae derelicti infidelitatem, quae cordis obdurati genuinam prolem pepererunt, et per eam a corpore Ecclesiae defracti suo merito perierunt.
pass_a: To all these let it be added, that when some nation, for example of the Jews, has been broken off from the body of the Church on account of unbelief, yet no one of the elect is broken off: for, by the same Apostle as author, a remnant according to the election of grace has been made safe, Rom. 11:5, 7. Finally, that certain ones are not broken off, others from the same nation springing back and perishing, that happens not because these were elected from foresighted faith of theirs, but because faith was given to these elect from the eternal good pleasure of God, and a reservation according to election was made, Rom. 11:5. So also that certain ones are broken off, by means of their unbelief, and perish, that does not argue that God from eternity reprobated them on account of foresighted unbelief; but that these reprobated, left to their own hardness, brought forth unbelief, the genuine offspring of an hardened heart, and through it, broken off from the body of the Church, perished by their own desert.
pass_b: Add this: when a nation — say the Jews — is broken off from the Church's body for unbelief, still none of the elect is broken off. By the same Apostle, a remnant according to the election of grace is saved (Rom. 11:5, 7). That some are not broken off while others of the same nation spring back and perish happens not because these were elected from foresighted faith, but because faith was given to these elect from God's eternal good pleasure, and a reservation according to election was made (Rom. 11:5). So too, that some are broken off by their unbelief and perish does not prove God from eternity reprobated them for foresighted unbelief. It proves that these reprobate, left to their hardness, brought forth unbelief — the genuine child of an hardened heart — and through it, broken from the Church's body, perished by their own desert.

lemmas.gloss: Rom. 11:5, 7 remnant by election of grace
reprobates left to hardness; unbelief follows
